comparator.name: Information Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The redesigned programme has 60 EC in each of the first two years. Year three comprises 30 EC of minor space and 30 EC of required ethics, AI, data science and thesis work. The example follows the programme for September 2026 entrants.
components: Humane AI in Digital Societies: Introduction
Humane AI in Digital Societies: Projects

core: Applied AI, data science, software and information processing
Human-centred information technology, interaction and evaluation
Language technology, search, natural-language processing and conversational AI
Responsible information processing and AI in society
adjacent: Business information science and digital organisations
questions: How can data, software and AI extract and organize useful information?
How can information technology be designed around people and evaluated responsibly?
How do language, search and conversational systems support human communication?

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

alternatives.label: AI, information and human-centred technology
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, databases and machine learning with the study of how people use technology and language. Courses in robotics, design and psychology help students examine how systems work for people.
alternatives.labelReason: Programming and brain and behaviour precede later software, AI and cognition courses. Data handling precedes machine learning and deep learning. The active offering for Psycholinguistics is in the second semester.
progression: Programming and brain and behaviour precede later software, AI and cognition courses. Data handling precedes machine learning and deep learning. The active offering for Psycholinguistics is in the second semester.

alternatives.label: Law, AI and digital governance
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, data and AI with law, public policy and ethics. It examines how institutions govern technology and how legal reasoning can inform decisions about its use.
alternatives.labelReason: Law, programming and methods precede institutional analysis, AI ethics, systems, machine learning and advanced legal courses. The law gateway precedes dependent courses.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, nine courses shift toward law and digital governance; compared with the business route, eight courses differ. Each pair therefore exceeds the 30-EC/four-course threshold.
progression: Law, programming and methods precede institutional analysis, AI ethics, systems, machine learning and advanced legal courses. The law gateway precedes dependent courses.

alternatives.label: Business information systems and AI
alternatives.concept: Combines software, databases and machine learning with business strategy, customer research and organisational behaviour. It explores how organisations use data and AI to make decisions and engage with customers.
alternatives.labelReason: Business, programming and databases precede software development, strategy and market research. Research methods support marketing, and introductory data science precedes later machine learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, seven courses shift toward business and organisations; compared with the law route, eight courses differ. Each pair therefore exceeds the 30-EC/four-course threshold.
progression: Business, programming and databases precede software development, strategy and market research. Research methods support marketing, and introductory data science precedes later machine learning.

selection.assessment: The closest option integrates information processing, AI, human-centred design and language. Law and IT and business information science are independently evidenced elective directions with substantial legal or organisational sequences. The three options meet the distinctness floor. AI and language are represented in the closest option, and the other named directions remain beyond the three-option limit.

blocks: Both teach relational database design and SQL. Groningen also develops database-driven web applications.
Both teach data cleaning and manipulation. UCR also introduces data visualisation.
Both teach machine-learning methods and model evaluation.
Both study neural networks and text applications. Groningen gives dedicated attention to language models and translation.
Both introduce programming and computational problem solving.
The selected UCR courses cover parts of information science. Groningen introduces it as a discipline.
UCR covers software and databases. Groningen teaches web development as a separate subject.
UCR algorithms and optimisation teach general search methods. Groningen studies search engines and information retrieval.
UCR logic, mathematics and data science supply foundations. Groningen separately studies information measures and encoding.
UCR studies AI models and optimisation. Groningen separately develops and evaluates work produced through human collaboration with generative AI.
UCR data courses include applied projects. Groningen requires a separate data science project.
Both investigate user needs and develop prototypes. UCR works with consumer products, while Groningen tests computer interfaces.
Both analyse linguistic choices and textual data. UCR focuses on stylistics, while Groningen connects linguistic theory to language technology.
UCR studies social aspects of technology across several subjects. Groningen gives humane AI dedicated interdisciplinary study.
The UCR courses include projects in design, ethics and AI. Groningen integrates these concerns in a dedicated humane AI project.
UCR Psycholinguistics investigates human speech and language. Groningen teaches computational processing of speech and language.
UCR Robotics studies movement, planning and manipulation. Groningen teaches spoken interfaces and evaluation of human-robot interaction.
Both introduce statistical analysis and inference. UCR applies these methods to business and social research.
Both examine ethical questions about technology. UCR focuses on AI, while Groningen covers information technology more broadly.
The Groningen thesis is required. UCR independent research is optional and appears separately.

notes.text: UCR offers related study in software, data, AI, language and technology use. Groningen gives more dedicated attention to web development, search engines, speech technology and human-robot interaction, and requires a data science project and thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Information Science at the University of Groningen combines applied AI, data science and language technology. Students study how to build information systems and evaluate how they serve people and society.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines AI and data with language, design and behaviour. Two related options focus on law and technology governance, or on business information systems.

componentNotes.y3-minor: Students can use this 30 EC space for a minor or combine a 15 EC Information Science placement with 15 EC of minor courses.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: The thesis requires at least 120 EC, including all first-year courses.
